title: Alcohol
intro: The Prophet (SAW) called alcohol “the mother of all evils”. The Qur’an forbade it step by step.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: Allah (SWT) says: O believers, intoxicants, gambling, idols and fortune-telling arrows are filthy things, the work of Shaytan – so stay away from them, so that you may be successful. Shaytan wants to stir up hostility and hatred between you through alcohol and gambling, and to keep you from remembering Allah and from prayer. So will you not stop? <small>(Qur’an, Al-Ma’idah 5:90–91)</small>

One of the goals of all the rules of the Shari‘ah is to raise people – and whole societies – who are healthy in mind and body. This goal is reached by protecting the values Islam treats as untouchable:
Because alcohol, like most modern addictions, harms all of these values, the Prophet (SAW) called it “the mother of all evils”.

Drinking wine and alcohol was very common among the Arabs before Islam. Allah (SWT), in His great wisdom, knew how harmful alcohol is, so as the Qur’an was revealed He forbade it gradually. This shows how widespread and accepted it was, and how hard this addiction is to treat. The Qur’an’s step-by-step way can help with treating alcoholism (the illness of being addicted to alcohol) and other problems our society faces.

items: a) Getting ready: in one ayah, intoxicating drinks are mentioned separately from “good food” – a wise hint that they are not good. Allah says: from the fruits of date palms and grapevines you make intoxicants and good food. (Qur’an, An-Nahl 16:67)

b) First step: alcohol is put alongside harmful things, so a person who cares about their health thinks about it: they ask you about wine and gambling – say: in them is great sin and some benefit for people, but their sin is greater than their benefit. (Qur’an, Al-Baqarah 2:219)
c) Second step: believers must not come to prayer while intoxicated, until they know what they are saying. (Qur’an, An-Nisa 4:43) This was not yet a total ban, but it prepared the way for it.
d) Third step: the complete ban, in ayahs 90–91 of Surah Al-Ma’idah: stay away from it! Will you not stop?

learn.text: Staying away from all of it

learn.html: The Prophet (SAW) cursed ten people connected with alcohol: the one who makes it, the one it is made for, the one who drinks it, the one who carries it, the one it is carried to, the one who serves it, the one who sells it, the one who profits from it, the one who buys it, and the one it is bought for. (Tirmidhi)
Because every contact with alcohol is forbidden, a Muslim is advised to avoid gatherings and places where alcohol is served or found.

learn.title: Hadith
learn.html: The Prophet (SAW) said: “Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him not sit at a table where cups of alcohol are passed around.” (Ahmad)

Sadly, there are Muslims who do not drink, but still sell alcohol and keep it in their homes, shops and hotels. Feeding a family with money earned in a haram way brings them under the curse mentioned in the hadith.
The ban is complete even when alcohol is used as a cure. The Prophet (SAW) said: “Allah has sent both the illness and the cure, so treat yourselves, but not with forbidden things.” (Abu Dawud)

learn.title: ⭐ Remember
learn.html: Alcohol is a great evil and a great sin – so avoid everything that has to do with alcohol.

practice.title: How the Qur’an forbade alcohol
practice.prompt: Put the steps in the right order.
items: Intoxicants are mentioned separately from good food (An-Nahl)
Their sin is greater than their benefit (Al-Baqarah)
Do not come to prayer intoxicated (An-Nisa)

practice.title: What would you do?
practice.prompt: You are at a friend’s party and you see alcohol being served. Tap every good choice, then tap Check.

options.text: 🚪 Politely leave or move away from that table
📞 Call your parents to pick you up
🥤 Drink only water or juice you know is halal
🧑‍🏫 Afterwards, talk about it with your teacher
🍺 Just take one sip to fit in
options.why: Every contact with alcohol is forbidden – even a little.
The one who serves alcohol is among the ten the Prophet (SAW) cursed.

questions.q: What did the Prophet (SAW) call alcohol?
Why did the Qur’an forbid alcohol gradually?
options: Because it was very common and hard to give up

questions.q: In which surah is the final, complete ban?
How many people connected with alcohol did the Prophet (SAW) curse?
May alcohol be used as a medicine?
options: No – we must not treat ourselves with forbidden things

questions.q: Is it allowed for a Muslim to sell alcohol if they don’t drink it?
options: No – the seller is also cursed

practice.title: Questions, tasks and talking with your teacher
prompts: 💬 Which values does Islam protect, and how does alcohol harm them?
📖 Describe the Qur’an’s steps in forbidding alcohol.
🔟 Which ten people did the Prophet (SAW) curse in connection with alcohol?
💊 Is alcohol allowed as a medicine?
🎉 Task (choose one): you are invited to a friend’s party and you know alcohol will be served. What will you do? Write your answer and talk about it with your teacher.
🏠 Task (choose one): you notice someone in your close family drinks alcohol. What will you do? How and with what words would you talk to them?
🛒 Task (choose one): what would you do if an adult sent you to buy alcohol? Write your answer and explain it.
